First read the specific BLS directions: the objects and outputs of clinical care, pathology and imaging reports and population prevention can differ, then verify the target jurisdiction's education, licensure, training and position conditions, and do not infer authority or tasks from the classification name.

Editorial observation suggestion: first understand the objects and training of the specific direction, then observe patience with long-term learning, verifying evidence as required and communicating. For clinical directions, also learn about patient care and procedural training; public health and similar positions may have different outputs, and difficult clinical work is not written as a necessary preference for all personnel.

Editorial observation suggestion: verify whether the target position's training period, exposure environment and responsibility match expectations; where there is clinical work, also verify occupational protection and personally tolerable conditions. Sensitivity or discomfort should be discussed with professionals in the specific setting, and this page does not determine that a person cannot work in the field.

Low-risk verification: complete the fictitious referral record check for D-03 on this page, listing the two blank fields of allergy history and previous treatment and the four conflicts of patient, tooth position, appointment and sender, and write the handover note pending verification. This only observes verification and communication preferences, does not diagnose, design treatment or handle real patients, and does not prove clinical ability or licensure.

Decision center: clarify the specific specialty's service objects, outputs and one's own education and licensure; use verifiable materials to understand record, communication and training requirements.

Insufficient evidence: O*NET has no work context data for this residual classification. The BLS dentists broad group describes clinic and other settings and different specialties; the clinical posture, referral and scheduling descriptions on this page are editorial questions pending verification only, and public health, teaching or reporting directions may differ, so actual positions must be read.

In the United States, general dentists, orthodontists, oral and maxillofacial surgeons and prosthodontists have their own codes; dental hygienists, assistants and the laboratory are separate. Duties and individual licences may overlap, and codes neither grant nor exclude specific procedural authority. Verify training, the target jurisdiction and institutional conditions, and do not swap full licences by similar names.

Inputs that must be verified: the referral form and previous treatment records, chief complaint and history (including systemic disease, medication and allergy history), imaging and specialty examination findings, treatment plans and alternatives, informed consent, the isolation and protection conditions required for specialty procedures, and follow-up arrangements. What must not be done: do not perform specialty procedures without practice qualification or beyond registration scope, do not operate on experience when specialty evidence is insufficient, do not omit informed consent and medical records, and do not omit instrument sterilization, isolation and radiation protection procedures.

Fit judgments should combine specialty mentoring observation, difficult case discussion and follow-up outcome feedback, and are not replaced by an interest type or a single test; manual dexterity, image interpretation ability, and the willingness to bear the pressure of difficult cases and complications must be confirmed in real training and feedback.

All paper exercises on this page use fictitious materials; real specialty examinations and procedures, anesthesia and prescribing, radiological examination and surgery, and medical record and privacy handling are carried out by licensed and registered physicians with the corresponding specialty training and authorization under the applicable jurisdictional regulations (such as mainland China's Physicians Law and the practice requirements for the dental category, and U.S. state licence requirements) and unit policies.

The specific work of this classification varies by specialty: BLS introduces endodontics, periodontics, paediatric dentistry, oral pathology, imaging and public health directions separately, and clinical care, diagnostic reports and population prevention can have different objects and outputs. The referral, examination, consent, procedure and follow-up below are editorial clinical scenarios that apply only to the corresponding clinical positions and cannot be treated as a uniform official task list for the residual classification.

Check one: whether referral information and previous records are complete — whether the purpose of referral, previous treatment, imaging and medication history are clear; missing items must be obtained from the referring physician or patient, and treatment must not be continued on impressions.

Check two: whether specialty examination and imaging support the specialty diagnosis — whether clinical findings and imaging appearances are consistent, and whether additional examinations or consultation are needed; irreversible specialty procedures must not begin on insufficient evidence.

Check three: whether treatment goals and alternatives are clearly explained and consent obtained — whether expected outcomes, course of treatment, risks, costs and alternatives are explained to the patient and informed consent recorded.

Check four: whether the procedures are within specialty registration scope and one's own ability — whether anesthesia, medication, specialty surgery and highly difficult procedures fall within one's registration scope and trained ability; when beyond it, refer or involve a supervising physician according to the process.

Check five: whether isolation, protection and equipment conditions meet the requirements of specialty procedures — whether isolation such as rubber dam, the condition of microscopes or dedicated equipment, personal protection and imaging protection are carried out according to standards.

Check six: whether outcome evaluation, follow-up and return are a closed loop — whether outcome indicators, recall arrangements, complication identification and return conclusions are recorded and sent back to the referring physician, and whether anomalies and adverse events are reported as required.

Where are the boundaries between this residual classification and general dentists, other dental specialties, dental hygienists and laboratory technicians?

This table compares the U.S. residual classification with adjacent occupations in terms of objects, processes and outputs, with examples by specific direction. General dentists, orthodontists, oral and maxillofacial surgeons and prosthodontists have independent codes; hygienists, assistants and the laboratory provide care, support and manufacturing respectively. Occupational tasks may partially overlap, and individual authority follows the jurisdiction and institutional conditions, so full licences cannot be swapped by code or name.
Core purpose

Each specific specialty forms outputs such as clinical care, diagnostic reports or population prevention according to its service objects; this classification does not define a uniform difficult-case loop.

Core purposes of adjacent and specialty positions: general dentists provide diagnosis and treatment of common oral disease; orthodontists correct malocclusion; oral and maxillofacial surgeons provide maxillofacial surgical care; prosthodontists provide complex prosthodontics and occlusal reconstruction; dental hygienists perform licensed examination, scaling and preventive procedures; dental assistants provide chairside assistance; dental laboratory technicians fabricate restorations to prescription.
Main objects and basis

Editorial verification: does the specific position serve individual patients, report recipients or population programmes? The referral, examination or programme materials actually required and the applicable standards are verified separately, and the same inputs are not imposed on all positions.

Objects and basis of adjacent and specialty positions: general dentists focus on common oral disease (general dental practice standards); orthodontists on dentofacial malocclusion and growth (orthodontic standards); oral and maxillofacial surgeons on maxillofacial disease and trauma (surgical standards and surgical authorization); prosthodontists on missing teeth and occlusion (prosthodontic standards); dental hygienists on periodontal care and prevention (oral prevention standards and state licensure); dental assistants on the treatment process (infection control requirements); and laboratory technicians on work orders and impression or scan data (prosthetics process requirements).
Core process

Editorial clinical example: verifying referral materials → authorised examination and diagnosis → plan and disclosure → procedures within authorized scope and records → applicable follow-up or return. Public health and similar directions may differ.

Processes of adjacent and specialty positions: consultation, examination and treatment of common conditions (general dentists); impression and image analysis and appliance design (orthodontists); preoperative assessment and surgery (oral and maxillofacial surgeons); preparation, impressions and restoration fitting (prosthodontists); examination, scaling and preventive procedures (dental hygienists); chairside assistance and instrument handling (dental assistants); prescription-based fabrication and inspection of restorations (laboratory technicians).
Main outputs

Clinical directions can produce care and follow-up records; reporting directions can produce diagnostic reports; public health can produce prevention programme records. These are not a common deliverable for the same position.

Outputs of adjacent and specialty positions: records of diagnosis and treatment of common conditions (general dentists); treatment plans and stage-by-stage recall records (orthodontists); surgical and postoperative follow-up records (oral and maxillofacial surgeons); restoration and occlusion records (prosthodontists); periodontal examination and scaling records (dental hygienists); treatment assistance and sterilization records (dental assistants); restoration and inspection records (laboratory technicians).
Responsible party

The specific position bears responsibility for decisions, records and collaboration within its duties; the scope of individual licensure follows the jurisdiction and institutional conditions and is not determined by the U.S. classification name.

Responsible parties of adjacent and specialty positions: general dentists are responsible for the diagnosis and treatment of common oral disease; orthodontists, oral and maxillofacial surgeons and prosthodontists are each responsible for decisions within their specialty; dental hygienists are responsible for examination and scaling within their licence; dental assistants are responsible for chairside assistance and instrument handling; laboratory technicians are responsible for the quality of restorations fabricated to prescription.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with the referring physician, other specialties in the institution, dental hygienists, dental assistants and the laboratory; when cases exceed one's specialty scope or ability, or there are infection control hazards or equipment anomalies, pause the procedure, review the records and consult, refer or report according to unit policy.

Collaboration of adjacent and specialty positions: general dentists collaborate with the institution's departments and the laboratory; orthodontists and oral and maxillofacial surgeons collaborate with imaging, anesthesia and ward teams; prosthodontists collaborate with the laboratory; dental hygienists collaborate with dentists and patients; dental assistants collaborate with dentists and the front desk; laboratory technicians collaborate with physicians and quality staff.
Conclusion boundaries

The full licences of adjacent occupations are not interchangeable; specific tasks may overlap and must be verified against the target jurisdiction, training and unit conditions. The classification does not automatically exclude all adjacent tasks.

Examples for the oral pathology, oral radiology and public health directions: they form pathology diagnostic opinions, imaging diagnostic reports or population prevention programme records respectively; these three are not a common continuous process for the same position.

General dentists are responsible for the diagnosis and treatment of common oral disease; dental hygienists provide preventive care, examination and scaling and form care or nursing records respectively. Jurisdictional licences and tasks may partially overlap, and full licences are not interchangeable.

Orthodontists diagnose and correct dentofacial problems; oral and maxillofacial surgeons perform the corresponding surgical care, forming treatment and recall records or surgical and follow-up records respectively. Independent statistical codes do not directly determine an individual's full licence.

Prosthodontists diagnose, design and fit dental restorations; dental laboratory technicians fabricate and inspect restorations to prescription and specification, with clinical care and manufacturing quality being separate responsibilities.
Direction one within the occupation: preservation and regeneration specialties such as endodontics and periodontics

BLS describes endodontics as dealing with root canal problems and periodontics as dealing with the periodontium and supporting tissues. The specific surgical, microscopic or regenerative processes must be verified against the corresponding training and standards; this page does not list unverified special processes as uniform work.

The objects and training of each direction must be verified separately, and complexity, course of treatment, equipment or duration are not compared uniformly without a survey; different classification codes do not directly determine an individual's full practice authority.
If you are willing to do fine work over the long term and accept multiple recalls and follow-up visits, the preservation and regeneration specialty can be a medium- to long-term goal.
Direction two within the occupation: paediatric dentistry and care for special populations

Manage childhood dental disease and prevention during growth and development, carry out behaviour management and parent education, and provide accessible oral care for special populations such as people with disabilities or older adults.

Compared with adult specialties, it relies more on communication, behaviour management and family collaboration, and the treatment plan must be adjusted as the child grows; compared with general dentists, this direction requires additional training in child behaviour management and care for special populations.
If you enjoy communicating with children and families and can patiently handle uncooperative situations, you might consider the paediatric dentistry and special populations direction.
Direction three within the occupation: oral pathology, oral radiology and public health dentistry

The three can form pathology diagnostic opinions, imaging diagnostic reports or population prevention programmes respectively; they are not a continuous process for the same position, and documentation and programme conditions are verified against the specific position.
If you would rather work in diagnostic support, population prevention or teaching and research, you can move toward oral pathology, oral radiology and public health dentistry.
Adjacent occupations: general dentists (29-1021.00) and dental hygienists (29-1292.00)

General dentists are responsible for the diagnosis and treatment of common oral disease, and dental hygienists provide preventive care and the corresponding examination and scaling; licences and duties are verified separately by location. This residual classification may have different specialty objects and does not uniformly take on all referrals or mandate return.
If you want to handle a broader range of common conditions and take first-contact responsibility, compare general dentists; if you prefer prevention and patient education, compare dental hygienists.
Adjacent specialties: orthodontists (29-1023.00) and oral and maxillofacial surgeons (29-1022.00)

Orthodontics and oral and maxillofacial surgery have independent codes and corresponding training in the United States, providing correction and surgical care respectively; this statistical residual category does not include those codes, but individual full licences cannot be inferred from codes, and referral follows actual ability and the applicable system.
If you clearly want to do malocclusion correction or maxillofacial surgery, plan the education and training path for that independent specialty directly.
Adjacent occupations: prosthodontists (29-1024.00) and dental laboratory technicians (51-9081.00)

Prosthodontics is responsible for the diagnosis, design and fitting of restorations, while laboratory technicians fabricate and repair to prescription and specification. Manufacturing and clinical care are separate responsibilities; this page cannot describe the laboratory as having absolutely no patient contact, nor determine individual licensure from the classification.
If you prefer prosthodontic design and occlusal reconstruction, compare the prosthodontist path; if you prefer independent fabrication and inspection, compare the laboratory direction.

subject.name: Dentists, All Other Specialists
subject.summary: U.S. Dentists, All Other Specialists (O*NET-SOC29-1029.00) is a residual category for dental specialties not listed separately. BLS describes the endodontic, periodontal, paediatric, oral pathology, radiology and public health directions separately, and clinical care, reporting and population prevention can have different objects and outputs; the clinical process on this page is an editorial example, not a uniform official task. In the United States the median annual wage for this subcategory in May 2025 is 224,990 USD, with a median hourly wage of 108.17 USD. O*NET2024—2034 shows employment 6,600 → 6,600, growth 0% and 200 openings per year on average; BLS2025—2035 shows the same subcategory 5,800 → 5,900 with 1% growth, while the Dentists broad group grows 6% with 4,800 openings per year on average, each period and scope being explained separately. U.S. education and state licensure, mainland China physician qualification and registration, and the specific training and institutional conditions are verified separately. Insufficient evidence: the 2025 mainland China wage release consulted did not provide a dental specialty occupational distribution, and no AI effects, representative recruitment or task context materials were obtained for this residual category.
